'''Jamaal Eric Franklin'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.californiabirthindex.org/birth/jamaal_eric_franklin_born_1991_20609630|title=Jamaal Eric Franklin was born on July 21, 1991 in San Bernardino County, California|website=californiabirthindex.org|publisher=[[California Birth Index]]|access-date=May 8, 2020}}</ref> (born July 21, 1991)<ref>{{cite web|title=2012–13 SDSU men's basketball prospectus|publisher=SDSU Athletics|year=2012|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/sdsu/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/prospectus/prospectus.pdf|access-date=July 19, 2012|archive-date=December 26, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121226060320/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/sdsu/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/prospectus/prospectus.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Converge FiberXers]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA). Franklin played [[college basketball]] for [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]], where he was the [[Mountain West Conference]] Player of the Year as well as an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] in his junior season. He was selected with the 41st overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and spent two seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) with the Grizzlies and [[Denver Nuggets]]. Franklin played eight seasons in the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] from 2014 to 2022. He has also played in the [[NBA Development League]], Puerto Rico and the Philippines.

==Early life==
Franklin was raised by his mother, Felicia Price.<ref name=pucin>{{cite web |last1=Pucin |first1=Diane |title=San Diego State's Jamaal Franklin comes out of nowhere |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-xpm-2013-mar-21-la-sp-0322-jamaal-franklin-20130322-story.html |website=Los Angeles Times |access-date=September 25, 2023 |date=March 21, 2013}}</ref> He and Price moved from [[Los Angeles]] to the rural town of [[Phelan, California]], when he was aged eight.<ref name=pucin />

==High school career==
Franklin played four years at [[Serrano High School]] in Phelan then played a prep season at [[Westwind Preparatory Academy|Westwind Prep]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]].  As a senior at Serrano, he led the state of [[California]] in scoring at 31.7 [[points per game]] and was a two-time All-[[California Interscholastic Federation]] selection.  In his season at Westwind, he averaged 18.5 points and 6.3 [[rebounds per game]].<ref name=BIO>{{cite web | title = Jamaal Franklin bio | publisher = SDSU Athletics | year = 2012 | url = http://www.goaztecs.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/franklin_jamaal00.html | access-date = July 19, 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180315003609/http://www.goaztecs.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/franklin_jamaal00.html | archive-date = March 15, 2018 | url-status = dead }}</ref> Franklin was rated as the 24th-best shooting guard in the class of 2009 coming out of [[Serrano High School]] and had an [[ESPN.com]] grade of 90. Out of high school, Franklin was offered to play basketball at [[Long Beach State University]] and [[San Diego State University]].<ref name="BIO" />

Franklin played three different sports at [[Serrano High School]]: basketball, football (wide receiver and free safety), and track and field, where he was a state high jumper.<ref name="BIO" />

==College career==
[[File:Jamaal Franklin SDSU Aztecs (5420500335).jpg|thumb|right|Franklin tries to drive past [[Garlon Green]] of [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] in 2011]]
Franklin enrolled at [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] to play for coach [[Steve Fisher (American basketball coach)|Steve Fisher]].  As a freshman, he was part of arguably the best season in school history, along with teammates [[Kawhi Leonard]] and [[Malcolm Thomas (basketball, born 1988)|Malcolm Thomas]], as the Aztecs went 34–3 and captured a #2 seed in the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011 NCAA Tournament]].  Franklin averaged 2.1 points and 1.9 rebounds in 8.1 minutes per game.<ref name=BIO/>

In his sophomore campaign, Franklin was thrust into the starting lineup as the Aztecs returned only one starter.  He responded by averaging 17.4 points and 7.9 rebounds per game and leading the Aztecs to an unexpected shared regular-season title and a #6 seed in the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA Tournament]].  Franklin was named [[Mountain West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Mountain West player of the year]]<ref>{{cite news| last =Zeigler| first =Mark| title =Franklin, Fisher claim top MW honors | newspaper =[[U-T San Diego]]| date =March 17, 1989| url =http://www.utsandiego.com/news/2012/mar/05/franklin-fisher-claim-top-mw-awards/| access-date = July 19, 2012}}</ref> and was recognized nationally as an [[2012 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[Associated Press]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Two Mountain West Players Receive Associated Press All-America Honors | publisher = Mountain West Conference | year = 2012 | url = http://www.themwc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032712aad.html | access-date = July 19, 2012 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20130203232743/http://www.themwc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032712aad.html | archive-date = February 3, 2013 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

Franklin resisted the lure of the professional ranks and returned to San Diego State in [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]] for his junior season. He went on to average 16.9 points and 9.5 rebounds in 32 games.<ref name=draft>{{cite web|title=Jamaal Franklin Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jamaal-franklin-1.html |work=sports-reference.com |access-date=April 16, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130616003634/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jamaal-franklin-1.html |archive-date=June 16, 2013 }}</ref>

On April 12, 2013, Franklin announced he would forgo his senior season to enter the NBA draft.<ref name=earlydraft>{{cite web|title=Jamaal Franklin to leave SDSU early for NBA draft |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/Jamaal-Franklin-to-leave-SDSU-early-for-NBA-draft-041213 |work=Fox Sports |access-date=April 16, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130415104135/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/Jamaal-Franklin-to-leave-SDSU-early-for-NBA-draft-041213 |archive-date=April 15, 2013 }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Memphis Grizzlies (2013–2014)===
On June 27, 2013, Franklin was selected with the 41st overall pick by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in [[2013 NBA draft]].<ref name=grizzlies>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies active in 2nd round of draft, take San Diego State's Jamaal Franklin with 41st pick|url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/grizzlies-active-in-2nd-round-of-draft-take-san-diego-states-jamaal-franklin-with-41st-pick/|work=FoxNews.com|date=June 28, 2013|access-date=January 5, 2014}}</ref> On July 26, 2013, he signed with the Grizzlies despite not appearing for them in the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign second round draft pick Jamaal Franklin|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13900|work=InsideHoops.com|date=July 26, 2013|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref> During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2013–14 NBA Assignments |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html |work=NBA.com |access-date=October 1, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703151241/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html |archive-date=July 3, 2014 }}</ref>

In July 2014, Franklin joined the Grizzlies for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies announce 2014 Orlando Pro Summer League roster|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-announce-orlando-summer-league-roster-140630|work=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2014|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref> On August 31, 2014, he was waived by the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies waive Jamaal Franklin|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=16493|work=InsideHoops.com|date=August 31, 2014|access-date=October 1, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151004110608/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=16493|archive-date=October 4, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Zhejiang Lions (2014–2015)===
On October 7, 2014, Franklin signed a two-month contract with the [[Zhejiang Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jamaal Franklin signs with Chinese team|url=http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/2014/oct/07/sdsu-basketball-franklin-china-pope-als/|work=SanDiegoUnionTribune.com|date=October 7, 2014|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Zhejiang Guangsha sign Jamaal Franklin to replace Jonathan Gibson|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/137008/zhejiang-guangsha-sign-jamaal-franklin-to-replace-jonathan-gibson.html|work=Sportando.com|date=October 8, 2014|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref> On November 26, 2014, he signed a one-month contract extension with the Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jamaal Franklin of Guangsha could return to NBA in January|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/142663/jamaal-franklin-of-guangsha-could-return-to-nba-in-january.html|work=Sportando.com|date=November 26, 2014|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref> Later that day, he scored 53 points on 19-of-29 shooting in Zhejiang's 120–112 win over the Chongqing Flying Dragons.<ref>{{cite web|title=Regular Season Round 11: Chongqing FD – Guangsha L. 112–120|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2014/1126_15106_7304.asp?|work=Eurobasket.com|date=November 26, 2014|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Former San Diego State guard Jamaal Franklin scores 53 points in China|url=https://www.mwcconnection.com/san-diego-state/2014/11/26/7295387/former-san-diego-state-guard-jamaal-franklin-scores-53-points-in-china|work=MWCConnection.com|date=November 26, 2014|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref> On January 5, 2015, he left Zhejiang after appearing in 26 games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jamaal Franklin leaves Chinese team Zhejiang Lions|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/147412/jamaal-franklin-leaves-chinese-team-zhejiang-lions.html|work=Sportando.com|date=January 5, 2015|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref> Over those 26 games, he averaged 28.5 points, 6.2 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.9 steals per game.

===Los Angeles D-Fenders (2015)===
On January 21, 2015, Franklin was acquired by the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the NBA Development League.<ref>{{cite web|title=D-Fenders Acquire Jamaal Franklin|url=http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/150121_franklin/|work=NBA.com|date=January 21, 2015|access-date=October 1, 2015|archive-date=October 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002062328/http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/150121_franklin/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 21, he had a season-best game with 27 points and 13 rebounds in a loss to the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=D-Fenders Come Up Short Against Spurs|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20150221/AUSLAD/|work=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2015|access-date=October 1, 2015|archive-date=October 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002053238/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20150221/AUSLAD/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2015)===
On April 12, 2015, Franklin signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nuggets Sign Jamaal Franklin|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-jamaal-franklin|work=NBA.com|date=April 12, 2015|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the team later that day, recording one rebound and one assist in a 122–111 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Faried scores 30 points, Nuggets beat Kings 122–111|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20150412/SACDEN/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=April 12, 2015|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref> On July 13, 2015, he was waived by the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nuggets Waive Jamaal Franklin|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2015/07/nuggets-waive-jamaal-franklin.html|work=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 13, 2015|access-date=October 1, 2015}}</ref>

===Second stint in D-League (2015–2016)===
On August 29, 2015, Franklin signed with the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the Chinese Basketball Association,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/419112/Jamaal-Franklin-joins-Guandong-Tigers|title=Jamaal Franklin joins Guandong Tigers|work=Asia-basket.com|date=August 29, 2015|access-date=October 11, 2015}}</ref> but left the team before appearing in a game for them. On December 4, he was reacquired by the Los Angeles D-Fenders.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5076846|title=D-Fenders Acquire Jamaal Franklin|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=December 4, 2015|access-date=December 4, 2015}}</ref>

=== Shanxi Brave Dragons (2015–2016) ===
On December 18, Franklin parted ways with the D-Fenders and signed with the [[Shanxi Brave Dragons]] (Shanxi Zhongyu) of the Chinese Basketball Association.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/431802/Shanxi-Zhongyu-adds-Franklin-to-their-roster|title=Shanxi Zhongyu adds Franklin to their roster|work=Asia-basket.com|date=December 18, 2015|access-date=December 18, 2015}}</ref> On January 10, 2016, Franklin recorded 44 points, 10 rebounds and 20 assists in a 133–123 win over the Jilin Tigers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2016/0110_2929_2922.asp|title=Shanxi 133 – Jilin 123|publisher=EuroBasket|date=January 10, 2016|access-date=April 15, 2020}}</ref> He dominated the Chinese Basketball Association, averaging incredible numbers during his time with Shanxi. In 19 games, he averaged a [[triple-double]] with 33.9 points, 10.8 rebounds and 10.3 assists, in addition to 3.3 steals and 1.5 blocks.<ref name="Guayama">{{cite news|url=https://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/detalles.asp?r=10145#.VwjpCRMrKRs|title=Brujos firman a Jamaal Franklin|work=BSNPR.com|date=April 5, 2016|access-date=April 9, 2016|language=es}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Brujos de Guayama (2016)===
On April 5, 2016, Franklin signed with [[Brujos de Guayama]] of the Puerto Rican [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref name="Guayama" /> He left the team later that month after appearing in just four games.

===Third stint in China (2016–2017)===
In May 2016, Franklin re-signed with the [[Shanxi Brave Dragons]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/200293/jamaal-franklin-signing-one-year-deal-with-shanxi-zhongyu.html|title=Jamaal Franklin signing one-year deal with Shanxi Zhongyu|work=Sportando.com|date=May 24, 2016|access-date=July 5, 2016}}</ref> On November 14, 2016, Franklin scored 61 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists in a 125–104 win over the [[Beijing Ducks]].<ref name=cbatripledouble>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/217374/jamaal-franklin-recorded-a-triple-double-with-61-points-12-rebounds-and-11-assists-in-china.html|title=Jamaal Franklin recorded a triple double with 61 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists in China|publisher=Sportando.com|date=November 14, 2016|access-date=November 16, 2016}}</ref> Franklin's performance was the first 60-point triple-double in the history of the CBA.<ref name=cbatripledouble />

=== Sichuan Blue Whales (2017–2019) ===
In July 2017, Franklin signed with the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/500302/Jamaal-Franklin-joins-Blue-Whales|title=Jamaal Franklin joins Blue Whales|work=asia-basket.com|date=July 29, 2017|access-date=July 29, 2017}}</ref> He re-signed with the team in August 2018.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/543997/Franklin-re-signs-at-Blue-Whales|title=Franklin re-signs at Blue Whales|work=asia-basket.com|date=August 11, 2018|access-date=August 11, 2018}}</ref>

=== Shanxi Loongs (2019–2021) ===
On July 29, 2019, Franklin agreed to a contract to re-join the Shanxi team, which had been renamed the Shanxi Loongs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jamaal-franklin-signs-deal-overseas/|title = Jamaal Franklin: Signs deal overseas| date=July 29, 2019 }}</ref> On December 10, 2019, Franklin collected a quadruple-double with forty-two points, twelve rebounds, twelve assists and ten steals in a 110–114 loss to the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2019-12/10/c_138621161.htm|title=Xinjiang edges Shanxi 114–110 despite Franklin's 42 points display in CBA|date=December 10, 2019|website=xinhuanet.com|access-date=December 10, 2019|archive-date=December 10, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210200719/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2019-12/10/c_138621161.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> He averaged 30.1 points, 9.5 rebounds, 10.1 assists, 2.3 steals and 1.4 blocks per game. On September 12, 2020, Franklin re-signed with the team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Franklin re-signs at Brave Dragons |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/644320/Franklin-re-signs-at-Brave-Dragons |website=Asia Basket |access-date=September 12, 2020 |date=September 12, 2020}}</ref>

=== Shanghai Sharks (2021–2022) ===
In October 2021, Franklin joined the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the Chinese Basketball Association.<ref>{{cite web |title=上海男篮正式为外援富兰克林注册 首秀有望登场 |url=https://www.163.com/sports/article/GMGMHLHG0005877V.html |website=网易体育 |access-date=March 4, 2025 |date=October 17, 2021}}</ref> He played 40 games for the Sharks during the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.asia-basket.com/player/Jamaal-Franklin/210393|title=Jamaal Franklin|work=asia-basket.com|access-date=July 28, 2023|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He re-joined the Sharks for the 2022–23 season,<ref>{{cite web |title=上海队续约富兰克林 三外援均为非保障合同 |url=https://sports.sina.com.cn/basketball/cba/2022-08-04/doc-imizirav6751849.shtml |website=新浪体育 |access-date=March 4, 2025 |date=August 4, 2022}}</ref> but left after nine games.<ref>{{cite web |title=上海队官宣：外援比斯利和富兰克林离队 |url=https://sports.sina.com.cn/basketball/cba/2022-11-02/doc-imqqsmrp4636273.shtml |website=新浪体育 |access-date=March 4, 2025 |date=November 2, 2022}}</ref>

=== Converge FiberXers (2023) ===
On January 25, 2023, Franklin signed with the [[Converge FiberXers]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) to replace [[Ethan Rusbatch]] as the team's import for the [[2023 PBA Governors' Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Ramos|first=Gerry|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/converge-brings-in-new-import-jamaal-franklin-a793-20230125 |title=Converge brings in new import Jamaal Franklin|website=Spin.ph|date=January 25, 2023|accessdate=January 25, 2023}}</ref>

On July 28, 2023, Franklin signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the [[2023–24 NBL season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/franklin-joins-36ers-for-nbl24-campaign|title=Franklin joins 36ers for NBL24 campaign|work=adelaide36ers.com|date=July 28, 2023|access-date=July 28, 2023}}</ref> He was released by the 36ers on September 25, 2023, prior to the start of the regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Club statement: Jamaal Franklin |url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/club-statement-jamaal-franklin |website=Adelaide 36ers |access-date=September 25, 2023 |date=September 25, 2023}}</ref>

=== Guangzhou Loong Lions (2025) ===
On March 4, 2025, Franklin signed with the [[Guangzhou Loong Lions]] of the Chinese Basketball Association.<ref>{{cite web |title=官方｜欢迎“三双王”贾马尔-富兰克林加入广州龙狮 |url=https://news.zhibo8.com/nba/2025-03-04/67c70b1f3a5a4native.htm |website=直播吧 |access-date=March 4, 2025 |date=March 4, 2025}}</ref>
